name: meeple-as-card-off-v1
description: THE ISOLATION CONTROL FOR R15. Takes the cap and toll changes of the handoff-v2 arm - meepleCapPerColour 2 and slotToll 1 - WITHOUT R15 itself: meepleAsCard stays false, so a meeple can never be spent as a card and only ever buys its colour's action through a neighbour's board, exactly as under v1. This overlay exists because overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json changes three knobs at once (R15, the amended cap, the amended toll) and a result from it cannot say which of the three produced it. Running this arm and reading it against BOTH v1 (no knobs set) and the full meeple-as-card-v1 arm turns one three-way confound into two two-way deltas: this-against-v1 isolates what the cap and toll changes do on their own, and meeple-as-card-v1-against-this isolates what R15 adds on top of them. THE PREDICTION IF R15 IS WHERE THE VALUE IS. This arm should read close to v1 on the hook and the meeples-boxed count - a wider cap and a priced slot with nothing new to spend a meeple ON should mostly just let the supply sit deeper rather than circulate faster - and the full arm should be where the game actually changes. THE PREDICTION IF THE CAP AND TOLL ALONE ACCOUNT FOR MOST OF IT. This arm should already read most of the way to the full arm's numbers, and R15 would be doing less work than the design assumes. Read the meeples-spent-as-resources line specifically: under this overlay it should read exactly zero, because there is no resource use to spend a meeple on, which is the sanity check that the isolation actually isolated something. ⚠️ At this stage of the build the engine does not yet read meepleAsCard or slotToll, so this overlay currently behaves exactly like the shipped v1 loop at meepleCapPerColour 2 - that is expected and is not a result, and it is also why this arm and overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json will read identically until the engine work lands.
